evidenceAudit.scope: Woman with perimenopausal or menopausal symptoms: clinical diagnosis, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for vasomotor symptoms, vaginal oestrogen, non-hormonal options and premature ovarian insufficiency, using NICE NG23.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG23 as extracted gives no HRT doses, formulations or regimens, no non-hormonal drug doses, and no testosterone dose.
Cervical, breast and bone health follow-up details were not captured.
No Saudi menopause guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: In otherwise healthy women over 45 years with menopausal symptoms, perimenopause and menopause are diagnosed without laboratory tests. HRT is offered for vasomotor symptoms after discussing short-term benefits and risks: oestrogen with progestogen for women with a uterus, oestrogen alone for women without. Transdermal rather than oral HRT is considered for women at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Premature ovarian insufficiency is diagnosed under 40 years from raised follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) on two samples 4 to 6 weeks apart.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose clinically
actions: Diagnose without laboratory tests in healthy women over 45 years; do not use laboratory or imaging tests to diagnose menopause.

clinicalManagement.title: Individualised plan
actions: Adopt an individualised approach to investigation and management.

clinicalManagement.title: Offer HRT for vasomotor symptoms
actions: Oestrogen with progestogen if uterus is present; oestrogen alone if not; consider transdermal if VTE risk is increased.

clinicalManagement.title: Treat urogenital atrophy
actions: Offer vaginal oestrogen, including to women on systemic HRT; no routine endometrial thickness monitoring.

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Review efficacy and tolerability at 3 months and annually; give contraception information.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG23 as extracted gives no doses. It recommends combined oestrogen and progestogen for women with a uterus, oestrogen alone without a uterus, vaginal oestrogen for urogenital atrophy, cognitive behavioural therapy for low mood, and testosterone supplementation (off-label as of November 2015) for low sexual desire when HRT alone is ineffective; it advises against routine selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors as first line for vasomotor symptoms alone. Select preparation and dose per the hospital or menopause service protocol and product information. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Healthy women over 45 years with menopausal symptoms.
Under 40 years and FSH elevated on 2 samples 4 to 6 weeks apart.

teaching.scope: Woman with perimenopausal or menopausal symptoms: clinical diagnosis, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for vasomotor symptoms, vaginal oestrogen, non-hormonal options and premature ovarian insufficiency, using NICE NG23.
pitfalls: Ordering hormone tests to diagnose menopause.
Diagnosing premature ovarian insufficiency on one test.
keyPoints: Transdermal HRT has no greater breast cancer risk than baseline at standard doses.
Premature ovarian insufficiency needs two FSH tests.
